Espoir Ngabo

Green candidate for U.S. Representative, District 7, Harris County, Texas · Challenger

Information technology professional (Regional IT, BrandSafway)

Espoir Ngabo is the Green Party nominee for U.S. House, Texas District 7. He ran without opposition and advanced from the Green Party convention in March 2026, and he is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot alongside Democratic incumbent Lizzie Pannill Fletcher and Republican Alexander Hale. He works in information technology, and Community Impact reports that he came to Houston from Congo as a refugee at age 5.

Where Ngabo stands

Health care and prescription drug costs
Says he would co-sponsor bills like the Medicare for All Act to set up a single-payer universal health care system. Supports more funding for community clinics in TX-7.
Social Security and Medicare
Opposes privatizing Medicare or Medicaid.
Government accountability
Proposes a law tying congressional salaries to a multiple of the median income in each member's home district, and no pay for members during government shutdowns. Pledges to donate his excess salary back into TX-7.
Infrastructure (transportation)
Supports expanding the Safe Streets and Roads for All program for sidewalks and street safety, and protecting Federal Transit Administration bus funding for TX-7. Proposes participatory budgeting and a zero-fare transit pilot.
Social services
Supports permanently authorizing Summer EBT and says he would co-sponsor it. Supports after-school care, cooling centers and family services.

Background

  • Green Party nominee, U.S. House TX-7; advanced from the Green Party convention in 2026
  • Regional IT, BrandSafway (2023–present)
